item.text: {"classifications":[{"segment_id":"1","code":0,"rationale":"The President recites prior emergency declarations and factual background; this segment neither directs an agency nor itself creates a new legal consequence.","evidence":"The 2019 novel coronavirus known as SARS-CoV-2, the virus causing outbreaks of the disease COVID-19, has significantly disrupted the lives of Americans."},{"segment_id":"2","code":1,"rationale":"The President sets policy and directs the Secretary of Transportation to use existing authorities to expedite projects; any project action occurs later through discretionary agency implementation.","evidence":"the Secretary of Transportation shall use all relevant emergency and other authorities to expedite work on, and completion of, all authorized and appropriated highway and other infrastructure projects"},{"segment_id":"3","code":1,"rationale":"The Secretary of Transportation must submit periodic internal reports, and the Secretary of the Army must expedite projects under existing authority; no specified legal outcome is dictated.","evidence":"the Secretary of Transportation shall provide a summary report"},{"segment_id":"4","code":1,"rationale":"The named departments must expedite projects, identify possible NEPA pathways, report, and use lawful procedures; these are internal reporting and discretionary implementation duties rather than prescribed legal outcomes.","evidence":"the heads of all agencies are directed to use, to the fullest extent possible and consistent with applicable law, emergency procedures"},{"segment_id":"5","code":1,"rationale":"The Interior and Commerce Secretaries must circulate reports, while agency heads must use an existing emergency-consultation regulation to the lawful extent possible; consequences depend on later agency application.","evidence":"The heads of all agencies are directed to use, to the fullest extent possible and consistent with applicable law, the ESA regulation on consultations in emergencies"},{"segment_id":"6","code":1,"rationale":"Each agency head must provide an internal status report within the specified period, with no alteration of legal rights or required substantive agency result.","evidence":"the head of each agency shall provide a status report"},{"segment_id":"7","code":1,"rationale":"The agencies must distribute and periodically update internal status reports concerning their actions; this is executive reporting and coordination.","evidence":"Such status reports shall thereafter be provided to these officials at least every 30 days"},{"segment_id":"8","code":1,"rationale":"The Secretary of the Interior must ensure that a Service official is available for consultation and appropriate action, an internal availability and coordination assignment without a dictated outcome.","evidence":"shall be available to consult promptly with agencies"},{"segment_id":"9","code":1,"rationale":"The Secretary of Commerce must ensure that the fisheries official is available for consultation and other unspecified action; the remaining text introduces a later agency assignment.","evidence":"shall be available for such consultation and to take such other action"},{"segment_id":"10","code":1,"rationale":"Agency heads must identify potential actions that might qualify for existing emergency permitting treatment; the segment requires review and identification, not issuance of permits or exemptions.","evidence":"shall identify planned or potential actions"},{"segment_id":"11","code":1,"rationale":"Agency heads must report identified actions and use existing permitting provisions to the lawful extent possible; later applications remain agency-administered and are not predetermined here.","evidence":"The heads of all agencies are directed to use, to the fullest extent possible and consistent with applicable law, the emergency Army Corps permitting provisions"},{"segment_id":"12","code":1,"rationale":"Agencies must provide periodic status reports, while the Army Secretary must remain available for consultation and appropriate action; these are reporting and coordination duties.","evidence":"each agency shall provide a status report"},{"segment_id":"13","code":1,"rationale":"The EPA Administrator must cooperate promptly with the Army Secretary and agencies in administering the section, an internal interagency coordination requirement.","evidence":"The Administrator of the EPA shall provide prompt cooperation"},{"segment_id":"14","code":1,"rationale":"Agency heads must review existing legal and guidance authorities within 30 days; the review itself creates no legal consequence.","evidence":"shall review all statutes, regulations, and guidance documents"},{"segment_id":"15","code":1,"rationale":"Agency heads must identify potential actions eligible for expedited treatment under existing law; no waiver, exemption, or other outcome is granted or mandated.","evidence":"shall identify planned or potential actions"},{"segment_id":"16","code":1,"rationale":"Agencies must report identified actions and use existing authorities to their lawful extent, leaving particular outcomes to later agency implementation.","evidence":"agencies shall use such statutes and regulations to the fullest extent permitted"},{"segment_id":"17","code":1,"rationale":"Agencies must submit recurring status reports, and the general provisions preserve existing agency and OMB authority; these are internal reporting and housekeeping rules.","evidence":"each agency shall provide a status report"}]}
